scenario.title: THIRD BATTLE OF KHARKOV - 7 MAR 1943
intro.text:
THIRD BATTLE OF KHARKOV - 7 MAR 1943

South of Kharkov, Ukraine

We expect a German attack on Kharkov again. Stop the attack and inflict maximum losses on the enemy!

ORDERS
After 10 turns control 6/4/3 VH for a BV/V/TV.

CORE (recommended)
4x Tank
5x Infantry
2x Anti-Tank
3x Reconnaissance
2x Flak
4x Artillery
3x Fighter Aircraft
3x Tactical Bomber (+1)
header.act: ACT III — FROM DEFEAT TO OPERATIONAL MASTERY
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-briliant.text: Tatsinskaya burned, the transport rows disappeared, and the raiding column returned before the trap closed. Antonov has become unbearable for reasons I cannot dispute.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-victory.text: The airfield was wrecked and enough of the corps came home to remain a corps. The return route cost almost as much fighting as the objective.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-tactical.text: Eight formations escaped Tatsinskaya. Everything behind the eighth became the price of teaching the airlift that its rear was not safe.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-a.text: At Tatsinskaya you ordered the aircraft destroyed before the column turned. The crews proved what a raid can accomplish; the survivors also know exactly how late that order sent them home.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: The road you guarded at Tatsinskaya saved the raiding force as an organisation. Some aircraft escaped while we secured it, and Antonov has counted every one in arguments since.
line.earned-decision.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.earned-decision.text: Enough of the Tatsinskaya raiders returned together to be used as more than replacements. They have earned a choice about what happens to the formation they brought home.
line.earned-decision.choice.form-raider-: Re-form the returning raiders as a Guards infantry detachment.
Add an experienced eight-strength Guards infantry detachment to the core.
line.earned-decision.choice.distribute-r: Distribute their crews among the mobile formations.
Give tank and reconnaissance formations 20 experience and fully refuel the core.
line.earned-a-response.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.earned-a-response.text: The title will carry expectations as well as honour. They know what it means to attack beyond help and still return under their own colours.
line.earned-b-response.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.earned-b-response.text: The raid will survive as trained crews rather than a badge. Every mobile regiment receives men who have already found a road home from an encirclement.
line.scene-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.scene-0.text: The staff table still carries the red arrows of last month's advance. Sokolova places blue counters across them one by one until the map tells a different story: exposed columns, tired infantry, and an enemy concentrating faster than expected.
line.scene-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.scene-1.text: Tatsinskaya taught the crews to live at the end of a fuel column. The winter advance taught too many headquarters to pretend there was no end at all.
line.decision.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.decision.text: We can insist on the city approaches and risk being fixed there, or conduct an elastic defence that preserves the army while surrendering ground command expected us to hold.
line.decision.choice.hold-the-approaches: Stand on the Kharkov approaches and make the counterattack pay for every objective.
Gain 100 prestige for holding the approaches and give infantry and artillery 18 experience each; receive no replacements.
line.decision.choice.elastic-defence.tex: Trade forward ground for organised counterattacks and keep the withdrawal routes open.
line.decision.choice.elastic-defence.hin: Restore every core formation to full strength, fuel, and ammunition and give tanks 15 experience; withdrawal transport costs 50 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-a-0.text: The line is held by reserves behind it as much as by troops on it. Every penetration gets a planned counterattack, not a general rush forward.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-a-1.text: The crews hear Kharkov and remember the road out last May. Give them a withdrawal hour now, before resolve becomes another order nobody can complete.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-b-0.text: Fallback lines are issued in writing, with times and road priorities. We withdraw formations, not survivors.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-b-1.text: The fallback lines are mine. If one formation leaves early, I answer for the gap; if headquarters forbids the movement, Orlov keeps the written order.
line.post-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.post-0.text: Kharkov has become a symbol twice over. Symbols do not protect flanks; staffs must.
